newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse picks up on improved demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse picks up on improved demand.

text.p: Trading at the Nairobi Stock Exchange picked up on improved demand for key shares on Monday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The 20-share index rose 15.92 to stand at 3,071.04. Turnover was posted at 14.630 million shillings traded on 283,130 shares from 21.580 million shillings traded on 410,896 shares.
Floor dealers and bourse officials said it looked like the market was picking up slightly having seen improved activity in the last quarter of the year.

"A lot of the trading that's been going on has been due to the share offers put out during the year," a senior broker said. "New offers attract new players into the market, who normally use their refund monies to re-invest in the market," he added.
Trading on the financials board was heavy with Kenya Commercial Bank trading 106,759 shares at 79 from 78 while National Bank of Kenya traded 23,075 shares at 13.50 from 13.45.
There was improved trading in the agriculturals, with Kakuzi moving 18,400 shares at 99 from 98 and Rea Vipingo trading 7,500 shares at 10.50 from 10.60.
Foreign investors transacted 3,300 shares of National Industrial Credit at 42 and some 300 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting at 141 from 142.

A broker said foreign investor participation in the market had improved by over 100 percent -- "It's very good because Kenya still seems to be an attractive destination for foreign investors," he added.
Kenya Airways gained five cents to close at 7.30 from 7.25, while Uchumi Supermarket was stable at 44 unchanged.
